docs.title: Deterministic workflow
read_when: designing workflow steps, transitions, gates, or actions
implementing start, finish, retry, or recovery behavior
deciding which workflow state is authoritative versus derived

docs.summary: Workflow progression is driven by authoritative declarative state and deterministic operations, not agent-authored orchestration. Step start activates, step finish completes, transitions are explicit, gates inspect separately from verify, attempts scope evidence, and durable effects resume instead of duplicating.

docs.title: Workflow kernel — Specification and Task execution
read_when: changing workflow, agent archetype or task type definitions
implementing start, finish, return, continuation or attention behaviour
wiring the Runtime, CLI or UI to Specification or Task execution
adding a step kind, an effect, an attention reason or a new subject
docs.summary: One deterministic workflow core drives both a Specification and each of its Tasks. Entry points only select the subject. Workflows, agent archetypes (preferred provider and a model per provider) and task types are project definitions. Each Task has its own type, workflow and preparation status (draft, ready, on-hold, cancelled), changed only by explicit decisions, a declared approval effect or its own escalation to the Specification. The Engine decides continuations; anything it cannot carry out is attention for the owner, derived from the state on every inspection and never stored. Canonical state lives in the Specification's `.execution/` folder, which lists the Task set; only the change journal is local. The kernel writes those files but does not commit them yet (follow-up F04).

docs.title: Record architecture decisions
docs.summary: Durable, cross-cutting decisions are recorded as lightweight numbered Markdown ADRs under docs/architecture/decisions/.

docs.title: Toolchain selection
docs.summary: The monorepo foundation is pnpm 10 + Turborepo + TypeScript + ESLint flat config (type-aware for TS) + Prettier + Vitest on Node Active LTS. Two versions are held back on purpose — pnpm (for GitHub Dependency Graph compatibility) and TypeScript (for the lint ecosystem) — each with an explicit upgrade condition.

docs.title: Branch and release model
docs.summary: main carries the next development version; short-lived feature/ and fix/ branches merge into it by squash-only PR; each maintained minor line has one long-lived release/vX.Y branch. The next-version choice (minor vs major) is always an explicit input.

docs.title: MIT license
docs.summary: The repository is licensed MIT — permissive, minimal obligations, sufficient for a public developer-tooling project. Provenance of any code brought in from another repository is checked per file when brought in.

docs.title: Repository tooling is separate from the product API
docs.summary: Repository-internal developer tooling lives under `tools/*` as private, unscoped packages and never becomes a Nevo SpecFlow product surface by default. Product capabilities are designed as `@nevo/*` packages and `nevo-specflow` commands in their own right.

docs.title: The product ships as a single bundled artifact
docs.summary: `@nevo/specflow` is distributed as one self-contained tarball. `nevo-repo-product` (esbuild) bundles the `nevo-specflow` entry, the internal workspace capability packages and `commander` into `dist/bin.js`, so the artifact installs with no registry and no workspace. Source package boundaries are unchanged — only the distribution is one file.

docs.title: Documentation architecture and taxonomy
docs.summary: Defines a documentation architecture that separates product behavior, durable system architecture, engineering guidance, reusable design-system knowledge, exact reference contracts, operational instructions, and a non-authoritative idea backlog, while using searchable scope, area, and tag metadata so discovery does not depend on folder paths alone.

docs.title: Product naming and surfaces
docs.summary: Names the product Nevo SpecFlow, its executable nevo-specflow, its long-lived backend Nevo SpecFlow Runtime, its interactive application Nevo SpecFlow UI, and keeps Nevo UI as the reusable design system.

docs.title: Product package build model
docs.summary: Product packages use extensionless TypeScript source imports and explicit neutral or Node package profiles. Reusable package JavaScript and declaration surfaces are bundled together with one tsdown-based library build, while repository tools keep raw NodeNext tsc output and the final nevo-specflow distribution remains governed by ADR 0011.

docs.title: Toolchain policy and version sources
docs.summary: Toolchain choices and upgrade constraints are durable architecture decisions, while exact installed versions are mutable dependency data owned by repository manifests, .nvmrc, workspace configuration, and the lockfile.

docs.title: Product artifact packaging and pnpm compatibility
docs.summary: Nevo SpecFlow keeps pnpm 10 while GitHub's documented Dependabot support stops at pnpm 10 and Dependency Graph still has an open multi-document-lockfile parsing gap, while keeping only the package-owned custom logic needed to build the self-contained product artifact and delegating archive creation to pnpm pack.

docs.title: Product package topology and dependency direction
docs.summary: Nevo SpecFlow is one npm-distributed local product composed from source packages. Product capabilities, including Runtime and UI, live under packages; apps is reserved for a future independently deployed or independently operated host. Package dependencies flow toward shared contracts and neutral foundations, with @nevo/specflow as the product composition root.

docs.title: Engine-owned scoped commits and protected branches
docs.summary: When Git is enabled, Specification Create commits its scaffold through one path-limited Engine commit capability that never commits on branches the project protects. Protection comes only from committed project configuration (git.commits); with Git disabled none of this applies.

docs.title: Feature-owned operation lists over a shared operation model
docs.summary: Operations are a shared entity (model, journal and registry index, per-kind adapters) read through feature-owned, read-only list routes registered by one helper. Specifications exposes GET /api/specs/operations, authorized by spec view; status comes from one documented table; freshness is by polling with ETag; there is no global operations index.

docs.title: The Specification manifest is the document registry; archetypes are project-defined catalogue entries
docs.summary: specification.yaml becomes the canonical registry of a Specification's documents (stable id, path, type) and records the selected archetype with a snapshot of its requirements. Archetypes and document types are project data files (ADR 0017), not compiled into the product. Frontmatter is optional and never authoritative; files outside the registry are unclassified. Structural completeness is a computed validation result.

docs.title: Document operations write files at once and land as Engine-owned path-limited commits through a durable queue
docs.summary: Amended by ADR 0018 (automatic commit is opt-in, default off). Every state-changing Specification document operation writes its files and registry change to disk immediately, answers once the content is durable and its commit request is durably queued, and lands in Git later as an Engine-owned path-limited commit executed by a per-checkout queue (one active batch per checkout, batches per Specification). Queued operations of one Specification consolidate into one commit; a batch save is one commit. The dirty window between write and commit is bounded and journaled; it relaxes the clean-checkout consequence of ADR 0013 for document operations only. Protected branches and commit blockers are checked before any file is written. Extends ADR 0013.

docs.title: Definitions are project data files read from the project configuration, never compiled into the product
docs.summary: Specification archetypes, document types and every later kind of definition (task archetypes, review kinds, ...) are YAML data files under .nevo/definitions/<kind>/ in the Project Home. The Engine reads definitions only from there, through a kind registry with a schema version and a JSON Schema per kind. The product ships default definitions as seed files used only to install them into a project. Nothing archetype-related is compiled in; deleting a file removes the definition for new work and existing Specifications keep their persisted snapshot.

docs.title: Engine commit policy per capability, the uncommitted-changes ledger and manual commit
docs.summary: A general policy decides per Engine capability whether its edits are committed automatically (default OFF, git.commits.auto.<capability> in project config with a local override, configuration only). With it off a write completes at once as uncommitted and is recorded in a durable, owner-keyed uncommitted-changes ledger in the durable core. A manual commit is the only way the Engine commits ledger content then: a normal operation through the same commit port, lease, claim algebra and journal, path-limited to the ledger paths of a scope, with the user's message, never arbitrary user changes. Abandoning a failed batch and policy-level auto-off are the same state. Create and definitions install stay always committed. Push is out of scope.

docs.title: One workflow kernel for Specifications and Tasks, per-Task types, agent archetypes and automatic continuation
docs.summary: Specifications and Tasks run through one deterministic workflow core and differ only in their entry points. Every Task has its own type and workflow, and the Specification archetype only restricts the types. Each step names a preferred agent archetype, which holds a preferred provider and a model per provider. A transition may continue automatically. When the Engine cannot resolve the next launch, the owner gets an attention item, derived from the state and never stored, instead of asking the agent. Canonical execution state belongs in Git in the Specification's .execution/ folder (written today, committed once follow-up F04 lands); only the change journal is local.

docs.title: Documentation discovery is a product capability
docs.summary: Documentation discovery is deliberately promoted into the product as `@nevo/specflow-docs`: it owns the frontmatter contract, deterministic discovery and optional semantic search, takes its taxonomy from a settings file next to the documentation, works without an initialized project, is exposed as the ordinary CLI command `nevo-specflow docs` and as the Runtime endpoint `GET /api/docs/search`, and keeps its index fresh on Runtime start and on read without a file watcher.

docs.title: Product-neutral AI semantic search engine
docs.summary: `@nevo/ai-semantic-search` is a product-neutral engine with embedding provider, chunk source and vector store ports, an OpenAI-compatible embeddings adapter with a probe, heading-aware versioned markdown chunking and hybrid BM25 + cosine ranking fused by reciprocal rank fusion. Its local index is disposable, file-backed, written atomically under a single-writer lock and rebuilt in full on any manifest mismatch; it uses no native modules and no provider SDK.
